events.title: The Nobel Peace Prize for Mother Teresa
events.shortBlurb: The Norwegian committee's choice fell on the nun of Calcutta, who received the world's most famous prize in the name of the poorest of the poor…
body: On 17 October 1979 the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that the Peace Prize would go to Mother Teresa of Calcutta, "for work undertaken in the struggle to overcome poverty and distress, which also constitutes a threat to peace."

She was born Gonxha Agnes Bojaxhiu at Skopje in 1910, had gone to India as a Loreto sister, and in 1946, on the train to Darjeeling, received what she called her "call within a call." The congregation she founded, the Missionaries of Charity, established at Calcutta on 7 October 1950, served the dying and the destitute of the city's streets.

At Oslo on 10 December she asked that the money for the customary banquet be given to the poor, and received the prize, as her own words had it, "for the glory of God and in the name of the poor." She died in 1997; John Paul II beatified her in 2003, and she was enrolled among the saints in 2016.
